hook
Black holes are the most extreme things in the universe. Not even light can escape them. But what are they, really?
birth
It starts with a giant star, many times heavier than our Sun. Fusion pushes outward, while gravity pulls inward.
collapse
When the star runs out of fuel, gravity wins. The core collapses, and the outer layers explode in a supernova.
density
What's left is unbelievably dense. Imagine squeezing the whole Earth down to the size of a marble.
space
Einstein showed that heavy objects bend space itself, like a bowling ball on a trampoline.
space
A black hole bends it so steeply, it creates a bottomless well.
horizon
Its edge is called the event horizon. Cross it, and you'd need to go faster than light to get back out. Nothing can.
light
Even light bends around it. Light that comes too close falls in and never returns. That's why it looks black.
disk
Gas swirling around it forms a glowing disk, heated to millions of degrees, sometimes outshining a whole galaxy.
time
And near a black hole, time itself slows down. One hour there could be years back on Earth.
photo
In 2019, scientists captured the first real image of one: a dark shadow, wrapped in a ring of fire.
outro
The death of a star, and a hole in space itself. Follow for more mind-blowing science!
